newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Bucaram threatens to fire school heads.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Bucaram threatens to fire school heads.

text.p: Ecuador's President Abdala Bucaram threatened Thursday to remove the authorities of schools whose students are fighting economic cutbacks.
But student groups defied the warning, saying they would continue to take to the streets to protest massive hikes in public service tariffs.

"Starting tomorrow, schools that protest will be tried and their presidents removed", Bucaram told reporters. "It's shameful that they are trying to kill childhood. In the country there are 2,300 schools, but only six in Quito, four in Cuenca and two in Ambato have adopted this stance -- all of them led by the Popular Democratic Movement (MPD)."
The MPD is a leftist party led by the National Teachers Union and the Federation of University Students.

University students leader Patricio Carrera denied the MDP was masterming the students' battle plan, and vowed protests would continue. "If everyone out there protesting were MPD supporters we would have won the presidential election," Carrera told Reuters.
Some 20 students and nine policemen have been injured and 150 arrested in week-long protests against government austerity measures.
